target_customer: State and local governments (counties) that refer patients and fund addiction treatment; Medi-Cal in-network patients
problem: Most addiction treatment is government funded but ineffective or lacks medical care; Recover offers medication plus counseling over telehealth at a claimed tenth of traditional program cost.
business_model: Government contracts and insurance reimbursement for telehealth addiction treatment (clinic entity Recover Medical Group P.C.)

founders.name: Nick Gulino
founders.background_notes: YC page: founded after family addiction experience. A directory snippet (theorg.com, not opened) says he worked ten years in addiction services and at McKinsey government practice; unverified.

competitors.name: Ophelia
competitors.funding_then: early funding, 2.7 million in an earlier startup announcement

technical_complexity.rationale: Telehealth delivery uses standard tools; the hard parts are clinical licensing, prescribing compliance and government contracting, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: County contracts and state certification (California DHCS certification, Medi-Cal in network per the company site) are slow to win and renew, but competitors like Workit and Ophelia offered similar care.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found. Better funded telehealth rivals raised large rounds in 2021 (Workit 118 million Series C in October 2021).

market_need_then: YC description cites over 20 million Americans with addiction and under 10 percent treated; governments fund most treatment, with high overdose death toll.

branding.domain_note: Uses letsrecover.com rather than recover.com, so the exact .com was likely not obtained; not sourced.

identity.voice_and_tone: mission-driven, personal founder story of family addiction

brand_strength.rationale: A generic dictionary word shared with other recovery brands, such as recovered.org; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Recover sells government-funded telehealth addiction treatment and remains active. Third-party profiles report only a small seed and roughly 3.3 million of 2024 revenue with about 22 staff, with no large outside round found. It grew on county contracts rather than venture capital, so the story is steady, capital-light growth with a risk concentrated in government contracts.
notes: A reported 130K seed in September 2021 (Springbank Collective per Village.ai) came only from aggregator snippets and one source, so it is not recorded as a round. Crunchbase page showed placeholder text. Revenue and headcount figures are from an aggregator. Outcome search found no shutdown, acquisition or layoffs. Rosenman Institute page could not be opened (rate-limited). Founder education and prior employers not found on opened sources. Ophelia source dated 2018 is an earlier-stage announcement.
